To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spectral width of stimulated Brillouin scattered radiation can be anomalously broadened by phase modulation of the exciting and scattered radiation pulses.

the spectral width (in Hz) of the stimulated Brilloun spectrum in a wavefront reversal configuration is larger by a factor of 1.5–1.6 (in our experiments, for a laser pulse duration of 0.5 ns) than that in a non-wavefront reversal configuration, and the spectral width of a stimulated Brilloun spectrum is proportional to the pulse duration.

the spectral width of a stimulated Brilloun scattering line excited by wavefront-reversed radiation pulses is anomalously broadened because of phase modulation of the radiation pulses caused by thermal absorption.

the Brillouin spectrum can be broadened significantly by the phase modulation of the exciting radiation pulse.
the Brillouin spectrum broadening in a wavefront-reversal configuration is a sensitive indicator for thermal absorption in the medium and can be used to estimate the absorption coefficient.
